title: What federal law allows to be excluded or exempted: non-narcotic over-the-counter drugs under 21 U.S.C. 811(g)(1) and the three exemption categories of 811(g)(3)
subtopic: Federal exclusion and exemption of preparations containing a controlled substance
rule_summary: Under 21 U.S.C. 811(g)(1) the Attorney General shall by regulation exclude any non-narcotic drug which contains a controlled substance from the application of subchapters I and II of chapter 13 of title 21 if such drug may, under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, be lawfully sold over the counter without a prescription. Under 21 CFR 1308.21(a) a person seeking to have such a nonnarcotic drug excluded from any schedule under 811(g)(1) may apply to DEA, and 21 CFR 1308.22 lists the nonnarcotic substances which may lawfully be sold over the counter without a prescription and are excluded from all schedules under 811(g)(1). Under 811(g)(3) the Attorney General may, by regulation, exempt any compound, mixture, or preparation containing a controlled substance from the application of all or any part of subchapter I if he finds that it meets the requirements of one of the following categories: (A) a mixture, or preparation containing a nonnarcotic controlled substance, which mixture or preparation is approved for prescription use, and which contains one or more other active ingredients which are not listed in any schedule and which are included therein in such combinations, quantity, proportion, or concentration as to vitiate the potential for abuse; (B) a compound, mixture, or preparation which contains any controlled substance, which is not for administration to a human being or animal, and which is packaged in such form or concentration, or with adulterants or denaturants, so that as packaged it does not present any significant potential for abuse; and (C) upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Health and Human Services, a compound, mixture, or preparation which contains any anabolic steroid, which is intended for administration to a human being or an animal, and which, because of its concentration, preparation, formulation or delivery system, does not present any significant potential for abuse. DEA's provisions on excluded and exempted substances and preparations are 21 CFR 1308.21 and 1308.22 (exclusion of nonnarcotic substances that may lawfully be sold over the counter without a prescription), 1308.23 and 1308.24 (exempt chemical preparations intended for laboratory, industrial, educational, or special research purposes and not for general administration to a human being or other animal), 1308.25 and 1308.26 (exclusion under 21 U.S.C. 802(41)(B)(i) of anabolic steroid products expressly intended for administration through implants to cattle or other nonhuman species), 1308.31 and 1308.32 (exemption under 811(g)(3)(A) of compounds, mixtures, or preparations containing a nonnarcotic controlled substance, listed as exempted prescription products), 1308.33 and 1308.34 (exemption of compounds, mixtures, or preparations containing an anabolic steroid, intended for administration to a human being or animal, that because of concentration, preparation, formulation, or delivery system have no significant potential for abuse) and 1308.35 (exemption of certain processed cannabis plant material and animal feed mixtures that are not used, or intended for use, for human consumption). Under 21 U.S.C. 802(17)(A) and (F) the term narcotic drug includes opium, opiates, derivatives of opium and opiates, and any compound, mixture, or preparation which contains any quantity of any of them.
exam_relevance: Tests the limits of a federal exception: an over-the-counter non-narcotic drug containing a controlled substance is to be excluded from the schedules, while an exemption under 811(g)(3) is available only for a nonnarcotic preparation approved for prescription use, a preparation not for administration to a human being or animal, or an anabolic steroid preparation found to present no significant potential for abuse, so a nonprescription preparation containing opium fits no federal exclusion or exemption category.

authority.name: Authority and criteria for classification of substances
Schedules of Controlled Substances: excluded and exempted substances and preparations

common_confusions: The exclusion in 21 U.S.C. 811(g)(1) is limited to non-narcotic drugs, and the exemption in 811(g)(3)(A) to nonnarcotic preparations approved for prescription use; a preparation containing opium, which 21 U.S.C. 802(17) makes a narcotic drug, fits neither.

Category (B) of 811(g)(3) is limited to preparations not for administration to a human being or animal, so for a preparation intended for administration to a human being the exemption categories are (A), a nonnarcotic preparation approved for prescription use, and (C), a preparation containing an anabolic steroid.
A preparation's listing in Schedule V, or its marketing as a nonprescription drug, is not an exclusion under 811(g)(1) or an exemption under 811(g)(3).
